title: Role-based Dashboard
what: The project's numbers and charts, laid out differently per role (Dev: Needs action, Sprint, Work pace, Testing, Bugs; QA: QC queue, Test results, Quality, Sprint; PO: Needs a decision, Sprint, Speed & forecast, Workload, Quality). Every number is clickable to see its ticket list.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click a number or a chart bar to open the ticket list
Narrow the numbers with the "Sprint" filter

keys: dashboard charts numbers chart kpi stats statistics

title: Dashboard section bar (quick jump)
what: A row of buttons stuck to the top of the dashboard, with the section in view highlighted; click to scroll to that section.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click the second section name in the section bar (e.g. Sprint): the page scrolls to that section
Click the fourth section name: the section in view is highlighted

keys: dashboard sections jump nav scroll section

title: Ask the AI about the dashboard numbers
what: The AI button on each card opens a chat about that report; the big button in the section bar asks about the whole dashboard. The AI gets the dashboard numbers (and QC results if any).

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click the "AI" chip on the "Needs attention" card (the "Ask AI about the whole dashboard" button in the section bar covers the whole dashboard)
at: Hỏi AI về Cần chú ý

how.t: Type a question about the numbers in the request box
how.at: Yêu cầu cho AI về các ticket đã chọn

how.t: Click "Send" (or Enter)

how: Wait for the AI's answer, then press Esc to close the panel

how.t: Click "AI history" in the sidebar
Choose the "Dashboard" tab to see the chat you just had

keys: ask ai dashboard ai numbers analysis anomalies

title: Needs attention
what: The role's key quick filters with counts, red (critical) or yellow (warning), items with a count first.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
In the "Needs attention" card click a row (e.g. "Blocked", "Overdue") to see the ticket list

how: Press Esc to close the side panel
keys: needs attention alerts warning blocked overdue critical

title: Long-running tickets / Waiting for test too long
what: Tickets sitting in the same state too long: yellow from the warning threshold, red past the bad threshold. You can choose which states to watch (QA watches the waiting-for-test states by default).

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
On the "Long-running tickets" card (QA: "Waiting for test too long") click the "State" button to choose the states to watch
Click the "… red / … yellow" chip to see the ticket list

how: Press Esc to close the side panel

how.t: Click a row in the card to open the ticket

keys: long running aging stale waiting for test too long stuck red yellow

title: Sprint KPIs, Sprint progress, Burndown
what: KPIs: Tickets in sprint (compared with the previous sprint), In progress, Awaiting QC, Sprint completion rate. Progress: a Done/QC/In progress/Todo bar with a time-elapsed marker and an On track/Slightly behind/Behind label. Burndown: actual, ideal and the forecast finish date.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click the "Tickets in sprint" KPI box (Sprint section) to see the tickets

how: Press Esc to close the side panel

how.t: Click the sprint's progress bar to see that sprint's tickets

how: See the Burndown card next to it: actual line, ideal line, forecast finish date
keys: kpi sprint progress burndown forecast completion rate on track behind

title: Tickets done per day, Lead time, Velocity, Moved across sprints
what: Tickets done per day (pick 7/14/30 days), Lead time (median, 85%, by Bug/Feature/Task), Velocity per sprint (PO; a carried-over ticket counts only in the sprint it closed), tickets moved across sprints several times.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
On the "Tickets done per day" card pick the range "7 days / 14 days / 30 days"
Click a bar in the chart to see the tickets done that day

keys: tickets done per day throughput lead time velocity moved sprint carry over time range

title: Work in progress (WIP limit), Awaiting QC by person, Open tickets by state
what: A table of each person's in-progress and Blocked tickets, with an "over limit" WIP warning; tickets waiting for QC by person; open tickets by state.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
On the "Work in progress" card choose a "WIP limit" of 2-5
Click a person's row to see their tickets

keys: wip limit workload over limit waiting for qc by person qa load

title: QC numbers: Test runs, First-pass, Returned, Reopened
what: Read from the state history: test runs, % passed on the first try, runs returned by QC, reopens; test results per day; by tester; returns by dev; tickets returned several times / reopened.

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click the "Test runs" box (Testing / Test results section) to see the tested tickets

how: Press Esc to close the side panel

how.t: Click the "Returned" box to see the tickets QC sent back to dev

keys: qc pass returned reopen first pass test runs testing ping pong by tester

title: Bug numbers
what: Bugs in sprint, New and fixed bugs per day, User bugs, Open bugs by priority and by module, Bugs vs Features, Not ready for sprint (PO).

how.t: Click "Dashboard" in the sidebar
Click the "bugs in sprint" number (the "Bugs in sprint" card) to open the ticket list

how: Scroll down: click a bar in the other bug cards (per day, priority, module, Bugs vs Features) to see the tickets
keys: bugs quality bugs by module bugs by priority bugs vs features not ready for sprint

title: Members page (one person at a time)
what: Pick a person to see their numbers for a period (Open, In progress, Awaiting QC, Blocked, Overdue, No update >7 days, Moved sprint ≥2 times, Done, Bugs, Lead time) and the Open / Needs attention / Done lists. Lead time leaves out bulk-closure days, like the Dashboard.

how.t: Click "Members" in the sidebar
Search with the "Search people" box
Click a person's name
Choose a "Period" of 7/14/30/60/90 days
Pick "Open" / "Needs attention" / "Done", then click a ticket to open it

keys: members people member person individual period

title: AI analysis of one person
what: The AI reads that person's tickets and numbers: Work summary, Review, Assessment, 1-1 prep, or your own request.

how.t: Click "Members" in the sidebar
Click a person's name in the list (or yourself)
On the "Ask AI about {name}" card click a button, e.g. "Work summary" (also "Review", "Assessment", "Prep 1:1")

how: Wait for the AI to finish, then press Esc to close the panel

how.t: Or edit the prompt in the request box (the default prompt follows the "Period" unless you edited it)
Choose "Tickets sent to AI": Open / Done / Both
Click "Analyze"

keys: ai analysis assessment review 1-1 one on one work summary performance

title: Compare the whole team + AI work split
what: Everyone side by side for a period (load bar, blocked / overdue / quiet >7 days, done count, lead time), sorted by Load / In progress / Risk / Done / Lead time; the AI analyzes the load and suggests how to rebalance work. Lead time leaves out bulk-closure days, like the Dashboard.

how.t: Click "Members" in the sidebar
Click "Whole team" at the top of the list
Choose a period of 7-90 days under "Period"
Pick the sort: Load / In progress / Risk / Done / Lead time
Click "AI work split"; the AI runs in the side panel
Press Esc to close the panel, then click a person to see their details

keys: compare whole team team compare team load split work rebalance workload

title: Open a ticket from a link (ticket chips on Telegram)
what: A link with ?ticket=VA-1 (e.g. clicking a ticket chip in Telegram) opens that ticket straight in the side panel; filters, page and project are in the URL too, for sharing.

how.t: Click "Tickets" in the sidebar: the page and filters show in the URL

how: Copy the current page URL to share the exact filters and page
Click a ticket chip in Telegram or open a link like /youtrack/?ticket=VA-123 to go straight to the ticket
keys: link ticket url share deep link telegram ticket chip

title: No token yet: opens Settings › YouTrack
what: Until a YouTrack token is pasted, opening the YouTrack tab switches to Settings › YouTrack to connect; there is no sample data.

how.t: Click "YouTrack" in the top bar: without a token the page switches to Settings › YouTrack by itself
Click the "Settings" icon at the right of the top bar
Choose the "YouTrack" section
Enter the "YouTrack URL"
Paste the "YouTrack token" (Profile → Account Security → New token)
Click "Save"

keys: no token not connected token youtrack connect settings mock
